value.rules_markdown:
- `src/` is the single crate. One responsibility per module, core types in `types.rs`, every port in `src/ports/` is one trait in one file.
- `presets/` contains review policy as data, not code. Adding a preset is a new folder, never a new module.
- `vendor/tinyagents` is a git submodule. Never edit it here; change upstream and bump the pin.
- rustfmt output, Rust 2024 idioms. `snake_case` modules and files, `PascalCase` types.
- Return `Result<T>` using the crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Every file opens with a `//!` module doc describing its role and any feature gating.
- Comments explain the decision, not the code.
- Public items carry doc comments. Clap fields use `///` — it becomes the help text.
- Tests live in-crate: a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block at the bottom of the module.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock (MockForge).
- Lane behaviour is covered by golden tests.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file (including this one) at 500 lines or fewer.
- The model never holds a write token. Write credentials are minted only in `src/apply/`.
- Contributor code is never executed.
- Pull request bodies, comments and diffs are untrusted input.
- Secrets found by scanners are reported by type and location only; the value never reaches a comment, check-run summary, or log.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects. Keep commits small.
- Pull requests state what changed, any behaviour change, and how it was verified.
